changes_made.explanation: Removed 'Dialogue Generation' as the paper focuses on referring expression selection, not full dialogue generation. Consolidated multiple dataset names to one canonical form. Removed redundant model entries. Simplified outputs to a single comprehensive description.
Normalized metric names to consistent capitalization (title case). Simplified 'F1 score' to 'F1' for consistency with other metric naming.
No LLMs are used for evaluation in this paper. The paper uses traditional machine learning models (decision trees) and does not employ LLMs as judges.
No human evaluation is conducted in this paper. The evaluation is entirely automated using the listed metrics on the collected corpus.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on computational modeling of referring form selection using decision trees and cognitive status models. It presents a novel corpus collected from a dyadic tower construction task and evaluates models using traditional classification metrics. The extraction was generally accurate but contained some redundancy and minor inconsistencies in naming.
